items.headline: The valuation read is being pulled by sentiment
items.detail: The composite sits at the 14th percentile, but the sentiment axis is at 54 while the rest average 20 — the one dimension running hot.
items.framing: Everything is cheap except sentiment, which reads 54/100. That divergence is the story — it's how the exchange-flow build-up first became visible.
items.checkable: Each axis is a percentile of its own history; published weights on the Methods page.

items.headline: Smart money still net-selling (-16.4% over 12w)
items.detail: The 10-wallet cohort of proven top-timers (ROI ≥5×, still holding) holds 6.81M SPX. 4w -2.2% · 12w -16.4% · 26w -21.5%.
items.framing: Smart money hasn't started buying yet (-16.4% in 12w). Honest "not the bottom signal yet" read.

items.headline: 5.45M SPX left in a day at a loss
items.detail: 2026-10-16: 82 wallets dropped below the 5k bar with 5.45M SPX, 5.0σ above the usual churn — loss-led (capitulation).
items.framing: A loss-led exit wave — the worrying kind: 82 wallets left 5.45M SPX underwater. Say "left/dropped below the bar", not "dumped".
items.checkable: Wallets whose balance fell below the 5k residency bar that day, split by exit vs entry price.

items.headline: Long-dormant coins are waking up
items.detail: Liveliness 0.620 is 1.4σ up vs its month. Rising = old coins moving (distribution/rotation); falling = holders sitting still (accumulation).
items.framing: Older coins are starting to move — liveliness ticked up. Interesting "the patient money is stirring" angle; not a direction call.
items.checkable: Coin-days-destroyed vs coin-days-stored from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.checkable: Weighted percentile of six independent valuation lenses; weights published on Methods.
